sentences.text:
Honourable Smt. Justice V.Sujatha
 Writ Petition No.29543 of 2023
Order:

The present Writ Petition came to be filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief:-
"...to issue an appropriate writ, order or direction more particularly one in nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondent No.4 in interfering with the petitioner rights over the land in an extent of Ac.0.50 cents in Sy.No.707/1 of Yerrakotala village, Kalakada Mandal, Annamayya District stating that the same belongs to government and the same required its children for playground that too without putting the petitioner on notice as arbitrary, illegal, contrary to the vell established legal principles apart from being violative of the fundamental and the Constitutional rights guaranteed to him under Articles 14, 19, 21 and 300A of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondent not to interfere with the petitioner rights over the land in an extent of Ac.0.50 cents in Sy.No.707/1of Yerrakotala village, Kalakada Mandal, Annamayya District without initiating the proceedings under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and pass....."
2. The petitioner has purchased the land to an extent of Acs.0.50 cents in Survey No.707/1 of Yerrakotala Village, Kalakada Mandal, Annamayya District through sale deed dated 27.03.2002 from one Pothuri Nagalakshumma.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Since the aforesaid date, the petitioner is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the subject land.

Thereafter, the petitioner has approached the Tahsildar,
Kalakada Mandal and intimated the acquisition of rights over the subject land, as it is contemplated under Section 4 (1) of the A.P. Rights in Land and Pattadar Pass Books Act, 1971, for incorporation in the Revenue Records and also to issue pattadar pass book and title deeds in his favour.

entities.text: Land and Pattadar Pass Books Act, 1971
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In pursuance of the same, the Tahsildar, having recognized the petitioner's possession over the subject land, mutated the revenue records and had issued pattadar pass book and title deeds in favour of the petitioner, duly after following the procedure envisaged under Section 5(3) of the Act, 1971 and the A.P. Rights in Land and Pattadar Pass Book Rules, 1989.

entities.text: Land and Pattadar Pass Book Rules, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. While the things stood thus, the respondent No.4 started digging holes on 01.11.2023, in the subject land in order to place the fences stating that the same belongs to Government and is required for playground to children.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner, with the help of neighboring land owners, made the 4th respondent leave from the subject land.

The main grievance of the petitioner is that the 4th respondent has neither issued any notice stating that the land is required for the purpose of playground nor paid compensation, but, in turn had tried to erect fence through the subject land without adhering to the procedure envisaged under the provisions of the K Babu vs The State Of Ap on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44508132/
1 Act, 2013.
4. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for School Education.
5. Today, when the writ petition came up for hearing, learned Government Pleader produced a copy of instructions of the District Educational Officer, Annamayya District, Rayachoti, wherein it is stated that the MPPS Gollapalli School building and playground are not located in the petitioner's survey number i.e. Sy.No.707/1 but are located in Sy.Nos.705 and 706.

entities.text: K Babu vs The State Of Ap
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further stated that the 4th respondent has not encroached the land in Sy.No.707/1 and further stated that the respondents are not interfering with the petitioner's land located in Sy.No.707/1, Gollapalli of Ek Palli, Kalakada Mandal.

6. In view of the admission made by the respondents in their written instructions that they have not interfered with the possession of the petitioner's land, this Court feels it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition by directing the 4th respondent not to interfere with the possession of the petitioner's land admeasuring to an extent of Acs.0.50 cents in Sy.No.707/1 of Yerrakotala Village,
Kalakada Mandal, Annamayya District.
7. Accordingly, with the above direction, this writ petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
JUSTICE V.SUJATHA Date : 17.11.2023 KGR HONOURABLE SMT.
